chunks.title: CLO 2024.1 - Color Matching Editor
chunks.content: # CLO 2024.1 - Color Matching Editor This document explains the updated features and usage instructions for the Color Matching Editor in CLO 2024.1, focusing on flexible color and material management through flag colors, material linking, and property editing. --- ## Overview of the Color Matching Editor in CLO 2024.1 This section introduces the revamped Color Matching Editor in CLO 2024.1, detailing the updated menu structure and how to access the editor. It explains the concept of flag colors and their role in managing different materials and properties for garment components. - From CLO 2024.1, the Color Matching Editor has an optimized function structure for more flexible use. - The main menu structure has been improved; access the editor by clicking **Production** in the top menu, then selecting **Color Matching Editor** from the drop-down. - Add a new color matching setup by clicking the **plus (+)** sign in the upper right corner. - The editor allows changing colors, textures, and material properties such as fabric physical properties, button shapes, and thread types. - Different material properties can be applied to different flag colors for versatile design creation. --- ## Adding and Managing Flag Colors This section covers how to add new flag colors, configure material types, and understand the default settings upon reopening the editor. - Click the **Add** button (right side) to open the window for adding a new flag color. - The window displays materials currently used, categorized by material types like fabric, stickers, etc. - Users can customize settings and options for each module based on their needs before adding a new flag color. - Use the **Unify Materials** button to unify classifications or individual material buttons for separate settings. - Hover over the icon in the upper right corner to view detailed material properties and link settings. - The **Handbook** button at the bottom links to official documentation. - Each click on **Add** inserts a new flag color; **Add and Close** adds the flag color and closes the window. - When reopening the window to add more flag colors, all options reset to default material settings. - Naming conventions are recommended for clarity; e.g., naming a flag color "Material" to differentiate it. --- ## Editing Material and Property Settings This section explains how to modify fabric textures, material attributes, and utilize the property editor for detailed adjustments. - Change main fabric textures or other material properties such as color and type using the property editor. - After adjustments, click **Update** to see the changes reflected in the 3D view. - Flag color modes include **Material**, **Link**, and **All Properties**, each serving different purposes in design flexibility. - The **All Properties** mode allows showing different materials on the same paper style, useful for changes in button shape, sticker size, or orientation. - To adjust sticker direction or position, select the sticker in the 3D window, then modify angle and position in the Attribute Editor after unlinking these parameters from the flag color.

chunks.title: CLO 2024.1 - Color Matching Editor
chunks.content: - After adjustments, click **Update** to see the changes reflected in the 3D view. - Flag color modes include **Material**, **Link**, and **All Properties**, each serving different purposes in design flexibility. - The **All Properties** mode allows showing different materials on the same paper style, useful for changes in button shape, sticker size, or orientation. - To adjust sticker direction or position, select the sticker in the 3D window, then modify angle and position in the Attribute Editor after unlinking these parameters from the flag color. --- ## Understanding Flag Color Linking and Copying This section details how to link flag colors to share material properties and how to modify linked materials. - The **Link** option copies a flag color scheme without changing its properties. - When creating a new flag color, select a material in the editor to link it, which highlights the linked material in yellow. - Changing one linked material (e.g., sleeve color) automatically updates all linked flag colors. - To remove link settings, right-click the color editor in the shrink chart and select either **Material** or **All Properties** for independent editing. - To link a new sticker across all flag colors, hold **Shift**, select the shrink chart, and drag the new sticker file onto the project file and main project page. --- ## Using the Object Window for Flag Color Management This section explains how to use the object window to display, activate, and inspect flag colors without opening the flag color editor. - Open and close all flag colors through the object window. - When enabled, all flag colors are listed below each object. - The **water drop icon** in the upper left activates flag color display for all objects; icons in front of each object toggle individual displays. - The current flag color being edited is highlighted with a white border. - Hovering over color blocks shows the names of all color matching options used by the object. - For **Material** type flag colors, color blocks show only the flag color name; for **Link** mode, all linked flag colors are listed. - **All Properties** type flag colors show a "Not Used" prompt if inactive. - Scrolling in the object window reveals color schemes for single projects and marks unused colors accordingly. - This method applies to fabrics, stickers, buttons, eyelets, threads, and sewing needles, enabling easy inspection without opening the editor. --- ## Enhanced Editing Operations and Workflow Tips This section covers workflow improvements such as drag-and-drop material application and shortcut keys for efficient flag color management. - Drag material documents (fabrics, stickers, accessories) from the object window to the 3D window, garment, or board to apply material properties. - Different textures and colors can be set for each applied color on the object. - To apply a project file with linked properties, drag the project file while pressing **Ctrl**, then release the mouse button; this applies the link property across all flag colors.

chunks.title: CLO 2024.1 - Color Matching Editor
chunks.content: --- ## Enhanced Editing Operations and Workflow Tips This section covers workflow improvements such as drag-and-drop material application and shortcut keys for efficient flag color management. - Drag material documents (fabrics, stickers, accessories) from the object window to the 3D window, garment, or board to apply material properties. - Different textures and colors can be set for each applied color on the object. - To apply a project file with linked properties, drag the project file while pressing **Ctrl**, then release the mouse button; this applies the link property across all flag colors. - Changes made to any flag color material in this linked state automatically update all linked flag colors. - To reset or remove link settings, right-click the color editor in the shrink chart and select **Material** or **All Properties**. - To apply a new sticker and reset all flag colors to link mode simultaneously, hold **Shift**, select the shrink chart, and drag the new sticker file to link it to the project file and main project page. - This enables synchronized color changes across flag colors. --- ## Project File Management and Version Compatibility This section highlights the importance of saving project files separately for version compatibility and stable workflow. - In CLO 2024, save the project file separately via **File > Save As** for compatibility with previous versions like 2024.0. - This ensures stable use of the Color Matching Editor functions and preserves settings for future editing. - The update enhances the QIYISER editor's features, making color matching more robust, convenient, and efficient. --- # Summary CLO 2024.1's Color Matching Editor introduces flexible flag color management, material linking, and enhanced property editing, improving garment design workflows. Users can easily add, link, and edit materials across flag colors, utilize the object window for quick inspections, and leverage drag-and-drop operations for efficient editing. Proper project file management ensures compatibility and stability in ongoing design work.
